bullets.title: Quad 2 macro regime intact: large-cap tech momentum vs. small-cap laggard
bullets.body: Hedgeye's macro framework stays in Quad 2 (growth+inflation accelerating), driving QQQ +4.2% last month vs. IWM -3.9%. USD +3.4% last month, WTI crude +29.1% on 3-month trend, CRB commodities +12.5%. All Mag-7 names carry bullish TREND signals except NFLX, which is bearish. S&P 500 immediate-term range cited at 7,701–7,880; 10-yr UST range 5.20–5.35%.

bullets.title: CPI watch: inflation expected to reaccelerate substantially Wednesday, rate-hike odds reset
bullets.body: Hedgeye expects the September CPI print (due Wednesday Oct 14) to show substantial acceleration above consensus. JPM's own monthly forecast pegs Oct 2026 headline CPI at 3.8% YoY (up from 3.6% in Sept) and core PCE at 3.0%. October rate-hike probabilities fell from ~60% to 15.5% post-last-print, a repricing Hedgeye says may not hold; 2-yr Treasury bullish with 4.75% lower bound, 30-yr at 5.2% floor.

bullets.title: MS CIO Wilson: favor quality + Capital Goods; equal-weight lagging cap-weight by 6%
bullets.body: Mike Wilson argues valuation and breadth are already discounting considerable tightening risk, with S&P forward P/E re-testing March lows near 19x. S&P Equal-Weight has underperformed cap-weight by 6% over six months and fell 5% in September when the 10-yr crossed 5%. Capital Goods stands out as revision breadth improved from 16% in February to ~40%; October CPI and Chair Warsh's IMF remarks are the next tests for whether financial conditions are doing the Fed's work.

bullets.title: S&P 3Q26 EPS growth +26.7% YoY; AI-centric names driving ~60% of index growth
bullets.body: Consensus expects S&P 500 3Q26 EPS growth of +26.7% YoY and revenue +9.9% YoY, both well above historical averages; full-year 2026 EPS growth of +28% would be the third-strongest year in over 20 years. Mag-7 contributes ~26% of SPX EPS growth while AI Tech ex-NVDA adds ~35%; MU, NVDA, and META are the top three single-name contributors. Consensus revisions have moved higher into results, potentially raising the earnings bar.

bullets.title: Anthropic analyst day Wednesday is single most important near-term AI catalyst
bullets.body: Multiple sources flag Anthropic's Wednesday analyst day as the key binary event for AI infrastructure names: ARR above $100bn exiting 2026 alongside falling token prices would validate the AI buildout thesis and be bullish for compute stocks. B300 spot prices hit a new high of $7.29/hr (+6.1%); NBIS raised rates to $9.00/hr, suggesting supply remains tight. A miss or leveling-off would trigger compute price 'catch-down' and depress 2029 capex expectations; peak AI lab ARR risk at $200–250bn vs. $400–600bn consensus would crush the Momentum factor.

bullets.title: AI capex/power shortfall intensifying; data center build well ahead of power delivery
bullets.body: ~65 IT GW of data center capacity is under construction (~140% of installed base) with ~361 GW announced (~760%); expected additions are 12.9 GW in 2026 and 18 GW in 2027, with many projects expected to face delays. Morgan Stanley is hosting a webcast on 'AI Power Shortfall, Implications for Semis and the Next AI Financing Wave.' Texas grid interconnect processes are on hold until the state's governor's race resolves (Abbott at 81% on Polymarket). CEG, VST, and TLN flagged as 'coiled spring' AI power names.

bullets.title: Semiconductors under pressure: AAPL cuts iPhone 18 Pro orders -15%, CXMT 4F memory threat hits MU -4%
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags Apple cutting iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max orders by 15% — described as the first meaningful downside signal to the bull case and unusually early post-launch. Separately, China's CXMT announced a 4F cell DRAM architecture with server rollout by end-2026, two years ahead of Samsung's 2028 goal; MU fell 4% on the news as SK Hynix and Micron have not announced 4F roadmaps. The semiconductor sector declined ~2% in premarket, KOSPI fell 3.7% overnight with SK Hynix -4.5% and Samsung -4.4%.

bullets.title: Memory super-cycle structural but cyclicality remains; MS prefers Compute & Networking over Memory
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's Shawn Kim shifts preference to AI Compute & Networking over Memory despite a 9x run in the latter, noting memory supply catch-up is unlikely in 2026 or most of 2027 due to capacity lead times. HBM prices are expected to more than double in 2027 as the industry shifts to HBM4; TSMC September sales rose 54.6% YoY. GPU rental prices remain elevated: B300 at $6.65/hr (spot), H100 +7.2% M/M to $2.83/hr. WFE cycle estimates: $200bn CY27 and $260bn CY28 (Wolfe).

bullets.title: OpenAI hits $50B ARR at 77% growth; AI enterprise velocity accelerating across the stack
bullets.body: OpenAI ended September at $50B annualized revenue run rate, up 77% in three months; B2B ARR doubled (+107%). ChatGPT reached 1.2 billion weekly active users. Anthropic launched Claude Haiku 5.5 at 75% lower cost than Haiku 4.5. TypeSafe raised $870M Series A at a $7.5B valuation for its System One AI decision model.

bullets.title: META surges ~4% on 'Watermelon' AI model speculation; Muse holds #1 App Store for 25 days
bullets.body: META is the best performer among Mag-7 today, up ~4% to ~$745, driven by speculation that a new AI model codenamed 'Watermelon' will launch next week following cryptic social posts by Zuckerberg and Chief AI Officer Alexander Wang. META Muse has held the #1 App Store position for 25 consecutive days and is described as the fastest-growing consumer AI app. Walmart is also partnering with META Muse on agentic commerce at a low-single-digit % commission.

bullets.title: MSFT scales Azure Maia to multi-gigawatt by 2027; custom silicon reduces NVDA dependency
bullets.body: Microsoft announced plans to expand Azure Maia custom AI chips to multi-gigawatt deployments starting in 2027. Maia 300 delivers 40% more tokens per megawatt versus leading GPU systems and 7x rack-scale token throughput versus Maia 200. CEO Nadella separately framed advanced AI models as 'insider threats' and called for emergency brake systems, a narrative Citi says warrants watching for cybersecurity implications.

bullets.title: 800V power narrative overstated; NVDA Rubin stays 54VDC, 800V pushed to Feynman ~2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues the 800V data center power narrative has been overstated: NVDA's Rubin platform is likely to remain 54VDC architecture, with true 800V rack power delivery pushed out to Feynman (~2028). OCP Summit this week is expected to provide clarity on 800V timing; sidecars and 2027 power centers are the near-term scale path. The 800V group has already re-rated to ~6.5x EV/NTM sales despite revenue growth accelerating from 12% to 27%.

bullets.title: Crude oil rallying toward $105–107; Saudi-Houthi escalation adds geopolitical bid
bullets.body: WTI crude is up ~2.1% to $93.74 premarket on Saudi-Houthi escalation, with tankers surging 2–4%. Hedgeye identifies Brent oil as a top long with a $107–108 upper range target, noting it's 'the best long on the board.' A separate analyst has a $120 WTI target. Hedgeye is maintaining a buy-dips posture; considering partial trims of energy longs near upper range boundaries.

bullets.title: Agentic AI disrupting hotel distribution; MAR/HLT/H best positioned, EXPE cautious
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues agentic AI is driving a 250–400bps shift to direct hotel bookings, expanding hotel REIT margins by 60–80bps and brand EBITDA by 3–9% above consensus by 2028. LLM search results link to official hotel sites 74–97% of the time vs. 8–13% on Google, favoring large loyalty programs. EXPE price target unchanged; BKNG unchanged at $230.

bullets.title: BofA flips CRM to Buy from Underperform with $285 PT; ADBE downgraded at Wells Fargo
bullets.body: BofA made a major ratings reversal on Salesforce, upgrading from Underperform to Buy and raising the price target from $160 to $285 (24% upside), citing AI momentum. Simultaneously, Wells Fargo downgraded Adobe to Underweight from Overweight, cutting the PT from $270 to $225; ADBE fell 3.9% premarket. Barclays also downgraded HubSpot to Equal-Weight.

bullets.title: NVDA and AMZN pursuing major AI acquisitions: Reflection AI and Decart respectively
bullets.body: NVIDIA is in early-stage talks to acquire Reflection AI and has already invested $800M in the startup. Amazon is in separate discussions to acquire AI startup Decart for ~$7B; the deal also involves Anthropic, NBIS, and NVDA. Separately, Schneider Electric is acquiring PTC for $23.7B (~8x CY27 EV/Sales), seen as a positive for vertical software vendors with agentic workloads.

bullets.title: Earnings vol cheap vs. recent realized; small caps show most pronounced discount
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley QDS flags that 4Q26 implied earnings moves of 4.7–4.9% are below 8-quarter realized moves across the Russell 1000, despite being at the 90th percentile on absolute basis. Small caps show the most pronounced vol discount with light futures positioning, low upside call premium, and dealers short gamma. Screened names with the best setups include CMCSA (100% hit ratio, 5.6% implied vs. 7.3% realized), WDC (-2.3% vol discount), and META (-1.1% vol discount).

bullets.title: Large-cap banks off 12% from August peak; financials earnings could re-rate NII + capital markets
bullets.body: JPM notes large-cap banks are down ~12% from mid-August peaks despite SPX/Nasdaq at records. 30-yr mortgage rates hit 7.40%, the highest since November 2023. C has +2.3% NII sensitivity and +6.4% 2026 EPS per 100bp rate rise, with trading revenue guidance raised to ~10% YoY. JPM derivatives strategy recommends XLF Oct 55.5/56.5 call spreads and C Oct 134/139 call spreads heading into earnings.

bullets.title: FSLR upgraded to Buy at Truist with $270 PT on stronger demand and Section 232 upside
bullets.body: Truist upgraded First Solar from Hold to Buy, raising its price target to $270 from $229, citing a stronger demand backdrop, anti-stockpiling measures under Section 232, and incremental upside from international production opportunities. FSLR rallied 2.5–2.9% with 63,689 option contracts trading (212% above the 30-day average).

bullets.title: Lithium prices decline on EU-China hybrid quota deal; ALB and SQM fall 4%+
bullets.body: An EU quota deal on Chinese hybrid vehicle exports (350k units annually) is expected to lift blended ASPs for Chinese NEV makers via product-mix upgrade and reduced dealer discounts, while a cut in NEV export VAT rebates from 13% to 9% (effective April 2027) adds only 1.6–2% of retail price impact. Lithium spot prices fell on the news, with ALB and SQM both down 4%+ in premarket.
